title: RossFast Non-Iterative Fast Richards Solver

primary_lineage.citation: Ross PJ (2003), Modeling Soil Water and Solute Transport—Fast, Simplified Numerical Solutions
primary_lineage.role: non-iterative continuity update and MFP-based approximate face flux

primary_lineage.citation: Ross PJ (2006), Fast Solution of Richards' Equation for Flexible Soil Hydraulic Property Descriptions
primary_lineage.role: flexible hydraulic-property extension; equation-level audit incomplete

primary_lineage.citation: Ross PJ (2011), Numerical Solution of the Continuity Equation for Soil Water Flow Using Precomputed Steady-State Fluxes
primary_lineage.role: precomputed accurate steady-Darcian face fluxes with bounded O(N) runtime linear solve

why_promoted: retains finite-volume continuity and exact computational mass balance
runtime has no global nonlinear iteration and uses one tridiagonal linear solve per internal step
face hydraulics can be generated from arbitrary h(theta) and K(h) relations offline
heterogeneous two-material paths are directly representable
runtime cost is largely independent of hydraulic-property complexity
architecture maps naturally to immutable shared material/geometry path tables and worker-local O(N) solve scratch

independent_evaluation.citation: Crevoisier D, Chanzy A, Voltz M (2009), Evaluation of the Ross fast solution of Richards' equation in unfavourable conditions for standard finite element methods, Advances in Water Resources 32(6):936-947

current_findings: Brooks-Corey is not a fundamental restriction of the broader Ross lineage
Ross 2011 provides a cleaner SWAP5 candidate than directly porting the 2003 approximate face-flux formula
the 2011 method is not iteration-free in offline table generation, but its production step contains no global nonlinear iteration
a global tridiagonal linear solve is compatible with the bounded runtime objective and should be distinguished from Newton iteration
table density, material/geometry class cardinality and saturated-unsaturated state switching remain qualification gates
full SWAP hydraulic catalog, accepted-step mass ledger, MODFLOW boundary duality and response tangent remain open
next_action: build an isolated Ross2011-style continuity/table prototype by reusing the existing SWAP5 Darcian face-oracle science where possible, then qualify exact mass, timestep bounds, saturated-unsaturated transitions and homogeneous/heterogeneous face tables before adding process sinks or groundwater coupling
